```{r, setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)

```

## 1) Download the Sample RNA-seq Count Matrix and associated Metadata.

```{r}

# Read in both data sets
count.df <- read.csv(file = "data/counts.csv", header = TRUE)
meta_data.df <- read.csv(file = "data/meta_data.csv", header = TRUE)
```

### Data wrangling over the next sequence of steps

```{r, message=FALSE}
# Use only 5 columns of data in the meta_data dataframe to make processing faster
metadata.modified <- meta_data.df %>%
  dplyr::select(1,10,23,29,41) %>%
  # The barcode variable will eventually be used to join the metadata to the count data
  # The hyphen in the barcode variable needs to be changed to a dot
  mutate(barcode = str_replace_all(barcode, "-", "."))

```

```{r, message=FALSE}

# Convert count.df to long format
# This is required for many of the ggplot graphs and many other functions in R
# Use the pivot_longer function to convert the count dataframe to one I am calling
# dat.long which will end up containing three columns - the Ensembl ID, one called
# Samples which will contain all of the individual sample values and one called
# Counts which will contain the gene_expression count values

dat.long <- count.df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -X,        # Pivot all columns except the one containing the Ensemble ID
    names_to = "Samples",    # Column name for your old wide headers
    values_to = "Counts"    # Column name for your data values
  )

```


```{r, message=FALSE}
# This code block is where I join the dat.long dataframe for the counts to the 
# metadata dataframe for the additional information needed for the assignment
# The results of the join are stored in a new dataframe.
# dat.long$Samples is joined on metadata.modified$barcode
dat.long.enriched <- dat.long %>%
  mutate(X = sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", X)) %>%
  inner_join(., metadata.modified, by = c("Samples" = "barcode"))

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# This code block is "experimental and will take additional work prior to submitting
# the final project. I wanted to be able to map the Ensembl IDs to their actual gene symbol
# I found the example on Google and have it working in my code. There are still some
# issues I need to resolve but overall, for several of the following plots - this
# translation makes a big difference.

# Load required libraries
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# The Ensemble ID has a "version" number on it that needs to be stripped off because
# the gene_symbols generated do not have it.
count.df.mod <- count.df %>%
  mutate(X = sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", X))

# Now need to pull the processed Ensemble ID's out into a vector
ensembl.ids <- count.df.mod %>% pull(X)

# This is the heart of the process where the Ensemble ID is mapped to Gene Symbols
gene_symbols <- mapIds(
  x = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys = ensembl.ids,
  keytype = "ENSEMBL",
  column = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first" # Keeps the first match if duplicate mappings occur
)

# Store the results in a dataframe "df" for use in a following join operation
df <- data.frame(names(gene_symbols),gene_symbols)

```
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# This is where I merge the previously created dataframe "df" that contains the
# actual mapping from Ensembl ID to gene using an inner join
dat.long.genes <- dat.long.enriched %>%
  inner_join(., df, by = c("X" = "names.gene_symbols."))

```

## 2) Gene selection and Summary Statistics

```{r, Q2}

# I am choosing the gene BRCA1 to study
# Using dplyr filter out only BRCA1 and do summary statistics
summary_stats <- dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  summarize(
    min = min(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Counts, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Counts, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
summary_stats
  

```
\newpage

## 3) Visualization

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# a) Create a Histogram: Use ggplot2 to generate a histogram of the count data for the selected gene.
# This visualization should effectively display the distribution of the counts.

dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=Counts, fill = ajcc_pathologic_stage)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.5, binwidth = 100) +
     labs(
        title = "Distribution of BRCA1 Gene Counts",
        x = "Sample",
        y = "Count (Frequency)"
  ) #+
    #facet_wrap(~ ajcc_pathologic_stage)
  
```
\newpage
```{r}

dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  group_by(ajcc_pathologic_stage) %>%
  summarise(total_value = sum(Counts, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x = ajcc_pathologic_stage, y = total_value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "cornflowerblue", color = "grey30") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "BRCA1 Counts by AJCC Pathologic Stage",
    x = "AJCC Pathologic Stage",
    y = "Counts"
  )
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# b) Create a Scatter Plot: Select a second gene from the dataset. Create a scatter plot using 
# ggplot2 to compare the count data of the two selected genes.

genes.of.interest <- c('BRCA1', 'BRCA2')

#df_test <- dat.long.genes %>%
dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols %in% genes.of.interest) %>%
  dplyr::select(-1) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene_symbols, values_from = Counts) %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=BRCA1,y=BRCA2)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(sample_type)), size = 1)

```
\newpage
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# c) Create a Violin Plot: Select one covariate from your metadata. Using the count data from the first 
   # gene and the selected covariate, generate a violin plot that illustrates the distribution of count 
   # data based on the covariate. For example, if you choose “primary_diagnosis”, your plot should display    # a violin plot for each level in “primary_diagnosis”.

dat.long.genes %>%
  filter(gene_symbols == 'BRCA1') %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=ajcc_pathologic_stage,y=Counts)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "skyblue", color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of BRCA1 Gene Counts by Stage",
    x = "AJCC Pathological Stage",
    y = "Count (Frequency)"
  ) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Heatmap annotations
column_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Disease_Status = meta_data.df.correct$ajcc_pathologic_stage,
  Laterality = meta_data.df.correct$laterality,
  col = list(
    Disease_Status = c("Stage I" = "red", "Stage IA" = "blue", "Stage IIA" = "green",
                       "Stage IIB" = "yellow", "Stage IIIA" = "brown", "Stage IIIC" = "gray"),
    Laterality = c(Left = "green", Right = "purple")
  )
)

```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Create heatmap
Heatmap(
  count.df.subset,
  name = "Counts",
  top_annotation = column_ha,
  #show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_row_names = FALSE,
  #show_column_names = FALSE,
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  column_title = "Samples",
  row_title = "Genes",
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Count")
)

```
